title: fix: make MCP base URL configurable
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes duplicate hardcoded MCP gateway URLs by using one `POLLINATIONS_BASE_URL` setting with `https://gen.pollinations.ai` as the default.
- Routes model-registry requests through the same configured base URL and documents local/self-hosted gateway usage.
- Makes the default no-key MCP smoke test offline-only; live registry and generation checks still run when `POLLINATIONS_API_KEY` is supplied.
- Bumps `@pollinations/mcp` to `2.4.0` so the fix can publish for production users (minor: the next npm release also ships the previously unpublished `listQuests` tool).
- Validated with Biome, an offline smoke test against an unreachable endpoint, a local HTTP override probe, `git diff --check`, and `npm pack --dry-run`.

gist.headline: One gateway, many gardens
gist.blurb: The MCP server has stopped carrying duplicate maps to the same hive. Point it at a local or self-hosted gateway with one setting, while the next release also brings along the previously unpublished quest-listing tool.
gist.summary: @pollinations/mcp 2.4.0 now uses a single POLLINATIONS_BASE_URL setting, defaulting to https://gen.pollinations.ai, for both generation and model-registry requests, with documented local and self-hosted gateway support.
gist.impact: MCP users can direct the server to a local or self-hosted Pollinations gateway without hardcoded URL conflicts, while production installs also receive the listQuests tool in the next npm release.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful little route planner connecting a cozy MCP terminal to two friendly garden gateways: the default gen.pollinations.ai hive and a small local garden-shed server. A single lime-green signpost labeled POLLINATIONS_BASE_URL directs both a model registry book and a generation spark down the same path; the eager CRT monitor robot can hold a tiny quest scroll.
